T0.scene_summary: A narrow bright kitchen with a stove on the left, cabinets and countertop on the right, and a potted plant beside a rear doorway.
T0.overall_evidence: The reconstruction captures the main galley layout, stove, colored cabinet fronts, plant, and rear opening. However, the viewpoint and framing differ substantially, the rear door appears much narrower, and several prominent surface textures and lighting cues are missing or simplified.

main_defects.description: The reconstruction is framed from a more centered, distant viewpoint: the stove occupies much less of the image, more of the rear wall is exposed, and a dark ceiling strip is visible where the reference shows none.
main_defects.evidence: The reference stove fills nearly the whole lower-left half, while the reconstructed stove occupies a smaller lower-left area; the reconstruction also shows a dark band along the top.
main_defects.uncertainty: Some apparent size differences may reflect object scale as well as camera placement.

main_defects.description: The rear opening or door appears as a very narrow vertical teal strip rather than the broad light-to-dark doorway visible in the reference.
main_defects.evidence: The reference doorway spans a substantially wider portion of the back wall and contains a bright upper region and dark lower region; the reconstruction shows a narrow uniformly dark panel.
main_defects.uncertainty: The reference door's exact opening angle and the space beyond it cannot be determined from the image.

main_defects.description: Surface detail and contrast are greatly reduced: the wood-grain floor becomes pale nearly uniform planks, the marble-like counter loses much of its veining, and dark or saturated finishes appear washed out.
main_defects.evidence: Wood grain is prominent across the reference floor, while the reconstruction shows mostly thin plank outlines; the reference stove body is near-black green, versus muted gray-green in the reconstruction.
main_defects.uncertainty: Lighting and exposure may contribute to the apparent differences in material color and contrast.

main_defects.description: The strong directional sunlight and sharp bright floor patch in the reference are absent, with the reconstruction instead showing broadly diffuse, flat illumination.
main_defects.evidence: A distinct diagonal bright patch crosses the floor in front of the reference doorway; no comparable patch is visible in the reconstruction.
main_defects.uncertainty: The different viewpoint changes the visible portion of the floor.

main_defects.description: The cooktop burners look like raised oval disks rather than flat circular markings, and the left-side unit and its visible handle are reduced to a thin strip beside the stove.
main_defects.evidence: The reconstructed burners have visible projecting edges, while the reference burners read as dark circles flush with the cooktop; the adjacent reference cabinet has a broad visible front and prominent vertical handle.
main_defects.uncertainty: The adjacent unit's apparent width is affected by viewpoint and occlusion.

strengths: The overall narrow galley arrangement is recognizable, with the stove to the left and a long counter and drawers to the right.
The stove retains six burner locations, a raised rear panel, two purple knobs, and a central clock display.
A slender potted plant stands near the back opening, and white upper cabinets and varied colored lower fronts are represented.
T0.uncertainty: This is an initial automated visual judgment based only on the two supplied images, not a human rating or validated aggregate metric. Camera, exposure, and occlusion can explain some apparent differences; hidden geometry is not assessed.

T1.scene_summary: A narrow galley kitchen with a stove on the left, counters and cabinets on the right, and a door and potted plant at the far end.
T1.overall_evidence: The reconstruction captures the main kitchen arrangement and recognizable appliances, cabinetry, plant and doorway. However, the more centered, wider view changes the apparent scale and angles of the objects, while simplified surfaces, altered door appearance and different lighting reduce fidelity to the reference.

main_defects.description: The reconstruction is framed more centrally and symmetrically, with the stove and rear doorway much smaller in the image and substantially more of the right-hand cabinetry and ceiling visible. The reference has a closer, more oblique view dominated by the left stove and the near right counter.
main_defects.evidence: The stove occupies roughly the left 41% of the reference width and extends nearly to the bottom, versus roughly the left 39% with a substantially smaller control panel in the reconstruction; the rear door and plant are also noticeably smaller.
main_defects.uncertainty: Some apparent size differences may also reflect scene proportions rather than camera placement alone.

main_defects.description: The reconstruction replaces the reference's visibly grained wood floor, metallic and dark textured stove, and veined counter surface with largely smooth, pale, low-contrast surfaces.
main_defects.evidence: Wood grain and strong tonal variation are prominent on the reference floor; the reconstruction floor is nearly uniform with sparse plank outlines. The reference stove has a dark body and reflective metallic controls while the reconstruction is flatter and lighter.
main_defects.uncertainty: Bright, diffuse illumination also contributes to the washed-out appearance.

main_defects.description: The reference shows a large light door leaf angled into the room with a dark edge and dark area behind it, whereas the reconstruction shows a narrow, flat dark vertical rectangle with a small knob.
main_defects.evidence: The visible door in the reference spans a broader area and has a slanted dark edge; the reconstructed feature is a thin front-facing rectangular panel.
main_defects.uncertainty: Perspective and lighting influence the apparent opening and color; hidden door geometry cannot be assessed.

main_defects.description: The strong directional light and sharp bright patch across the floor near the doorway in the reference are absent in the reconstruction, which is more uniformly bright and softly shaded.
main_defects.evidence: A distinct diagonal, high-contrast illuminated floor region appears in the reference but not in the reconstruction.
main_defects.uncertainty: The difference may result from a combination of light placement, exposure, and materials.

main_defects.description: The reference cooktop has six flat, inset-looking circular burner markings and a large angled control panel; the reconstruction's burner discs appear raised and overlapping in perspective, with a smaller, more upright panel.
main_defects.evidence: The reconstructed burner discs have visible raised edges and overlap visually, unlike the separated flush circles in the reference.
main_defects.uncertainty: Differences in viewing angle contribute to the apparent spacing and panel shape.

strengths: The major galley layout is retained: stove and short counter on the left, long counter and upper and lower cabinets on the right, and an open central aisle.
A plant sits near the back wall to the right of the door in both images.
The stove's six burner positions, two purple controls and central clock are recognizable, and the right cabinetry retains a mixture of pale and darker drawer fronts.
T1.uncertainty: This is an initial automated judgment from two rendered views, not human ground truth or a validated aggregate rating. Viewpoint, lighting and exposure can confound apparent differences in shape, scale and material; hidden geometry and support are not assessed.
